# Running

## Launch

```bash
sbatch TTpipe.sh                 # SLURM cluster
bash   TTpipe.sh                 # one machine (profiles/local)
bash   TTpipe.sh -n              # dry run: list the jobs, run nothing
sbatch TTpipe.sh --configfile config/mine.yaml    # a different (complete) config
sbatch TTpipe.sh --profile profiles/<site>        # override the compute profile
```

Every other argument is passed to `snakemake`, so the usual options work:
`-n` (dry run), `--until <rule>`, `-R <rule>` (rerun a rule and what depends
on it), `--forcerun`, and so on.

### What the launcher does

1. Works out the profile (`--profile`, then `$TTPIPE_PROFILE`, then
   `hpcProfile` in the config) and the output directory (a relative
   `outputDir` goes under `$TTPIPE_OUTPUT_ROOT`, else the folder you launch
   from).
2. Sources `<profile>/env.sh` (makes `python3` and `conda` available).
3. Creates a virtual environment `env/` the first time and installs
   `config/requirements.txt` (a pinned Snakemake and the SLURM plugin).
4. For SLURM profiles, sends the job logs to `<outputDir>/logs_slurm`.
5. Runs Snakemake with `--rerun-incomplete --keep-going`: a job interrupted
   half-way is redone, and one failed job does not stop the independent
   ones.

The launcher is itself a small SLURM job (1 CPU, 16 GB, 10 days; the memory
is for building conda environments on a first run). Each rule becomes its own
job. Building the environments first, in a separate step, and never two builds
at once, is described in
[Cluster reference](cluster.qmd#building-environments).

## Dry run

```bash
bash TTpipe.sh -n
```

Snakemake prints each job to be run, then a table of job counts per rule. It
also checks that input files exist (FASTQ files, the STAR index, the GTF), so
many path mistakes show up here, before anything is submitted. Dry runs send no
email.

For a samplesheet of *S* samples in *C* conditions with the defaults, the table
has: `fastqc` 2 x *S*; `star_align`, `mapq_filter`, `mark_duplicates` *S* each;
`split_strands` and `htseq_count` 2 x *S* each; `merge_bams` 3 x *C*; `bigwig`
3 x *C*; one each of `scale_factors`, `gene_info`, `count_matrix`,
`sample_table`, `deseq2`, `sankey`, `results_explorer`, `stranded_signal`, `qc_summary`, `qc_report`, `multiqc`; and
`rnk` per comparison (and `fgsea` per collection and comparison) when
`gsea_collections` is set. (`rnk` and `fgsea` appear only with GSEA
collections; `fastp`, `bigwig_sample` and `star_index` only when their switch
is on.) With the experimental `spike_in.enabled: true` there are also one
`spike_reference`, one `spike_idxstats` per sample, one `spike_summary`, and one
`spike_size_factors` when `normalize` contains `deseq2` and `run_analysis` is
true; with `spike_in.enabled: false` (the default) the job list is unchanged.

## What is running

| Stage | Rules | Notes |
|-------|-------|-------|
| Read QC | `fastqc` (and `fastp` if `trim: true`) | FastQC always runs on the raw reads |
| Alignment | `star_index` (if `build_star_index`), `star_align` | STAR with `--quantMode GeneCounts`; the temp BAM is deleted later |
| Filter | `mapq_filter`, `mark_duplicates` | MAPQ >= `min_mapq`; Picard removes duplicates |
| Strand and tracks | `split_strands`, `merge_bams`, `scale_factors`, `bigwig` | Forward and reverse BAMs; replicates merged for tracks |
| Counts | `gene_info`, `htseq_count`, `count_matrix` | Whole-gene counts per strand, then matrices |
| Statistics | `sample_table`, `deseq2`, `rnk`, `fgsea`, `sankey`, `results_explorer` | One DESeq2 job for all comparisons |
| Stranded page | `stranded_signal` (if `stranded_plots`) | Locus tracks, metagene profiles and antisense table from the stranded bigWigs |
| QC | `qc_summary`, `qc_report`, `multiqc` | Read the processing outputs |
| Spike-in (experimental, off by default) | `spike_reference`, `spike_idxstats`, `spike_summary`, `spike_size_factors` | Combined host + spike-in reference, spike-in pair counts in `spike/`, spike-in scale and size factors; spike-in genes go to `counts/counts_spike.txt`, not the host matrices |

[CODE_GUIDE.md](https://github.com/jpflores-13/TTpipe/blob/main/CODE_GUIDE.md)
describes every rule in detail.

## Monitoring

```bash
squeue -u $USER                         # your jobs
tail -f TTpipe-<jobid>.out              # the launcher's own log (Snakemake's progress)
ls <outputDir>/<sample>/logs/           # per-sample logs: one per job
ls <outputDir>/logs/                    # logs of the jobs that are not per sample
ls <outputDir>/logs_slurm/              # SLURM job logs
```

When a job fails Snakemake prints the failing rule, its log path and the
command. The logs per rule are `fastqc_R1.log`, `star_align.log`,
`mapq_filter.log`, `mark_duplicates.log`, `split_strands_forward.log`,
`htseq_count_forward.log` and so on, in the sample's `logs/` folder; the
DESeq2, fgsea, Sankey and QC logs are in `logs/`.

## Email notifications

With `TTPIPE_EMAIL` set (or `notify: email:` in the config), you get one mail
when the workflow starts, one when it finishes, and one if any job fails (with
the last lines of Snakemake's log). Not one per job, and none on dry runs. See
[Configuration](configuration.qmd#notifications).

## After a failure

```bash
bash unlock.sh            # release the Snakemake lock
sbatch TTpipe.sh          # --rerun-incomplete is on; finished steps are kept
```

The lock is left behind when a run is killed (for example by the wall-time
limit); `unlock.sh` accepts `--configfile` and `--profile` like the launcher.
Common failures:

- **Out of memory or time.** The per-rule numbers in the profile are guesses.
  Raise `mem_mb` or `runtime` for that rule ([Cluster
  reference](cluster.qmd#tuning-resources)) and resubmit.
- **Missing input.** A wrong `Sequencing_Directory` or file name, or a
  `star_index` that is not an index: the dry run shows these.
- **Zero or tiny counts.** FASTA and GTF with different chromosome names
  ([Setup](setup.qmd#the-chromosome-name-trap)).

## Rerunning after a change

Snakemake decides what to redo from file times and, by default, from changes
to a rule's parameters, input and code. So changing a config value that a rule
uses (for example `min_mapq` or `strandedness`) reruns that rule and what
depends on it, and changing nothing reruns nothing. Always look at the dry run
first: it shows what will be redone.

Snakemake also reruns a rule when the **conda environment file it uses
changes**, and it compares the whole file, so even editing a comment in
`envs/*.yml` triggers reruns of every rule that uses that environment (seen on
a real run: a comment-only edit made the dry run list the alignment and FastQC
jobs again). The dry run's "Reasons" section says "software environment
definition has changed". If that is not what you want, add
`--rerun-triggers mtime params input code` to the launcher command, which
drops the environment trigger.

## Running only part of the workflow

Three switches decide what runs: `run_processing`, `run_analysis`, `qc_report`
(at least one must be true). The graphs below are the rule graphs for the two
most common partial runs.

**Processing only** (`run_analysis: false`): everything up to counts, tracks and
the QC report, with no DESeq2, GSEA or Sankey.

```{mermaid}
%%| file: img/dag_processing.mmd
```

**Analysis only** (`run_processing: false`, with `analysis_counts` pointing at a
count matrix): the statistics and the report, with no alignment. The gene table
is still built from the GTF.

```{mermaid}
%%| file: img/dag_analysis.mmd
```

[Recipes](recipes.qmd) shows the config for each. These diagrams are
generated by `python scripts/make_dag.py` and must not be edited by hand.

## The finished output

When the last job ends you have, under `outputDir`:

- `qc/TTpipe_qc_report.html` (open this first), `qc/sample_qc.tsv`, and
  `qc/TTpipe_multiqc.html` on processing runs;
- per sample: BAMs, `stats/`, `counts/`, logs;
- `tracks/`, `merged/`, `counts/`, `analysis/`.

The STAR BAM, the MAPQ-filtered BAM and any trimmed FASTQs are deleted
automatically; the merged BAMs are kept. The full tree is in the
[README](https://github.com/jpflores-13/TTpipe#output-structure).
